newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek banks see drachma joining ERM in 1999 - poll.
newsitem.headline: Greek banks see drachma joining ERM in 1999 - poll.

text.p: The drachma will enter the exchange rate mechanism (ERM) of the European Monetary System in the spring of 1999 at an off-market rate, Greek bankers predicted in an informal Reuters poll.
A total of 25 banks participated in the informal poll which was conducted on April 11 and 14.
Bankers were asked the following questions:
Q1) When do you think the drachma will enter the ERM
Q2) Will it enter the ERM at a market rate or an off-market
Q1) YEAR SEASON VOTES TOTAL VOTES

To satisfy the exchange rate stability convergence criterion, a currency has to join the exchange rate mechanism (ERM) of the European Monetary System (EMS) and respect the normal fluctuation bands for at least two years prior to EMU participation.

Most EU currencies have been allowed to fluctuate by up to 15 percent on either side of their central cross rate since August 1993. The mark and the guilder are formally trading within the 2.25 percent band.
Bank of Greece governor Lucas Papademos said recently that Greece could join the EMU in 2000 or by the end of 2001 at the latest.
